prompt.context: The beverage department of a regional supermarket has seen a drop in revenue over the last year and has hired your firm to determine the cause of the decline and recommend ways to reverse the trend.
prompt.question: What is causing the revenue decline in the beverage department, and what recommendations would you make to reverse the trend?

clarifying_info.a: A leading regional grocer within the southeastern U.S.
No, the competitive landscape has not changed in the last year.

clarifying_info.q: Is the revenue decline across all product categories or specific to beverages?
clarifying_info.a: The revenue decline is specifically within the beverage segment.

clarifying_info.q: What does the client want from us?
clarifying_info.a: The client wants to find the cause of the declining revenue and recommendations for how to stop the decline.

exhibits.title: Revenues and Costs by Beverage Category
exhibits.shows: A table showing gallons sold (MM, average per store) and price per gallon ($) and cost per gallon ($) for three beverage categories — Sodas, Waters, and Others — for 2014 and 2015.

exhibits.title: Sodas by Brand
exhibits.shows: A table showing gallons sold (MM, average per store) and revenue ($M, average per store) for three soda brands — Brand A, Brand B, and Value Brand — for 2014 and 2015.

framework: Focus on revenue and its two levers: price and quantity (volume)
Segment revenue by category to identify where the decline is occurring
For declining categories, further segment by product/brand to isolate root cause
Avoid cost analysis — the problem is revenue-side
Generate recommendations using the 4Ps framework (Price, Promotion, Product, Placement) to reverse the decline

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, calculate total beverage revenue for 2014 and 2015 by category. Which categories are driving the overall decline?
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply gallons by price per gallon for each category and year, then compare. The key insight is that Sodas revenue has declined while Waters and Others have grown slightly. The overall beverage decline is entirely attributable to Sodas.

math.setup: Revenue = Gallons (MM) x Price per gallon ($)
math.answer: Sodas is the only category with declining revenue (-$6M). Waters and Others are growing. The overall decline is driven entirely by Sodas.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, calculate the implied price per gallon for each soda brand in 2014 and 2015. Which brand is causing the revenue decline in Sodas, and why?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate implied price = Revenue / Gallons for each brand. Brand A and Brand B both have stable implied prices of $1/gallon. The Value Brand's implied price has dropped from $0.60 to $0.40 — a 33% price cut. Volume for Value Brand surged (25M to 60M gallons), but the price cut more than offset the volume gain, causing revenue to decline. Brand A lost volume but maintained price.

math.setup: Implied price per gallon = Revenue ($M) / Gallons (MM)
steps: Brand A 2015: $30M / 30MM gal = $1.00/gal → Price unchanged; volume declined 40%
Brand B 2015: $30M / 30MM gal = $1.00/gal → Price unchanged; volume grew
Value Brand 2015: $24M / 60MM gal = $0.40/gal → Price cut 33%; volume tripled
math.answer: The Value Brand's price dropped from $0.60 to $0.40 per gallon. Although its volume tripled, this was insufficient to offset the price cut, contributing net +$9M in revenue but not enough to cover Brand A's -$20M decline. Brand A lost volume (possibly to the Value Brand) while maintaining its $1.00 price.

brainstorming.prompt: The client would like to hear your recommendations for how to reverse the decline in revenue of the beverage segment.

categories.name: Price
ideas: Raise the Value Brand price back toward $0.60 or an optimal price point that balances volume and revenue
Test price elasticity of Value Brand incrementally before committing to a full price change
Introduce tiered pricing or promotional pricing to stimulate Brand A volume recovery
Bundle pricing across brands (e.g., multi-pack deals) to drive higher average transaction value

categories.name: Promotion
ideas: Run targeted promotions to re-engage Brand A customers who may have shifted to the Value Brand
Loyalty program incentives tied to higher-margin soda brands
In-store advertising to highlight Brand A and Brand B quality differentiation vs. Value Brand
Seasonal or event-based promotions to drive volume for premium brands

categories.name: Product
ideas: Evaluate whether Value Brand should be repositioned or rebranded to reduce cannibalization of Brand A
Introduce new SKUs (e.g., flavored or functional variants) under Brand A or Brand B to attract incremental buyers
Consider private-label development at a sustainable margin if the Value Brand is the store's own label
Reduce shelf variety of Value Brand to manage volume mix

categories.name: Placement
ideas: Adjust shelf placement to give premium brands (A and B) more prominent eye-level positions
Reduce or move Value Brand to less prominent shelf space to discourage substitution from Brand A
Use end-cap displays for Brand A promotions to increase visibility
Optimize planogram to group brands by use-case (e.g., everyday vs. value) rather than side-by-side price comparison

recommendation: Adjust the price of the Value Brand upward — the 33% price cut from $0.60 to $0.40 per gallon is the primary driver of the soda revenue decline; restoring or optimizing the price is the most direct lever to recover revenue
Improve differentiation between Brand A and the Value Brand to reduce cannibalization and support Brand A volume recovery
risks: Raising the Value Brand price may alienate price-sensitive customers who switched to it, reducing volume gains achieved in 2015
Any changes affecting Brand A or Brand B pricing could strain supplier relationships
next_steps: Explore optimal pricing strategy for the Value Brand using price elasticity analysis
Explore bundling opportunities to increase average sales across soda brands
Explore marketing and in-store activities to differentiate the Value Brand from Brand A and Brand B
Explore shelf placement adjustments (planogram redesign) to reduce direct price-comparison between Value Brand and Brand A
